      Rigel Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

      News provided by

      Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

      Nov 05, 2026, 16:01 ET

      Share this article

        •

      Share this article

        •
      • Third quarter 2026 total revenues of $80.9 million, including net product sales of $72.3 million and contract revenues from collaborations of $8.6 million, and net income of $13.2 million
      • VEPPANU™ (vepdegestrant) became commercially available in mid-August and generated $6.6 million in initial net product sales for the third quarter
      • The Phase 1b study of R289, Rigel's dual IRAK1/4 inhibitor, in patients with lower-risk MDS is ongoing and Rigel expects to select the recommended Phase 2 dose by the end of 2026
      • Oral presentation at the ASH Annual Meeting in December will feature updated data from the ongoing Phase 1b study of R289 in patients with lower-risk MDS
      • Updated 2026 Outlook: Total revenues of approximately $290 to $295 million, which includes net product sales, excluding VEPPANU, of $255 to $260 million and contract revenues from collaborations of approximately $35 million
      • Conference call and webcast scheduled today at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time

      SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: RIGL), a commercial stage biotechnology company focused on hematologic disorders and cancer, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, including sales of TAVALISSE® (fostamatinib disodium hexahydrate), REZLIDHIA® (olutasidenib), GAVRETO® (pralsetinib) and VEPPANU™ (vepdegestrant).

      "VEPPANU's launch marks an exciting and transformational milestone for Rigel and we are very pleased with the initial uptake. In the first six weeks of launch we shipped VEPPANU to more than 100 patients and clinics and have already seen many refills," said Raul Rodriguez, Rigel's president and CEO. "Our priorities are to build on the VEPPANU launch and advance R289 in lower-risk MDS, with updated Phase 1b data to be presented at ASH in December. We believe VEPPANU and R289 have significant commercial potential to further transform Rigel and drive long-term shareholder value."

      Third Quarter 2026 Business Update

      Commercial

      • Third quarter net product sales were $72.3 million, an increase of 13% from the same period of 2025.
      • Year-to-date net product sales were $194.2 million, an increase of 17% from the same period of 2025.
      • Rigel announced that VEPPANU (vepdegestrant) became commercially available in the U.S. on August 13, 2026, generating $6.6 million in net product sales in the third quarter. VEPPANU is the first and only PRoteolysis TArgeting Chimera (PROTAC) approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of adults with estrogen receptor-positive (ER+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-), estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1)-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer (mBC), as detected by an FDA-authorized test, with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy.
      • Rigel's partner Knight Therapeutics Inc. (Knight) received regulatory approval from Colombia's Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos (INVIMA) in September for TAVALISSE for the treatment of adult patients with chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who have had an insufficient response, loss of response, or intolerance to prior treatment with corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin.
      • Knight announced it commercially launched TAVALISSE in Brazil in October.

      Clinical Development

      • Rigel continues to advance its Phase 1b clinical study of R2891, a potent and selective dual inhibitor of interleukin receptor-associated kinases 1 and 4 (IRAK1/4), in patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) lower-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and the company expects to complete enrollment and select the recommended Phase 2 dose for future development by the end of 2026.
      • Rigel announced that data from the ongoing Phase 1b study of R289 in patients with lower-risk MDS, including initial efficacy data from the dose expansion phase of the study, will be presented in an oral session at the 68th American Society of Hematology (ASH) Annual Meeting and Exposition in December. In addition, three poster presentations will include data for fostamatinib in patients with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) and warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (wAIHA).
      • The European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 featured data from the ARROW and TAPISTRY clinical trials of pralsetinib in patients with rearranged during transfection (RET) fusion-positive solid tumors in a rapid oral session. In addition, two poster presentations and an ePoster included clinical and health-related quality of life (HR-QoL) data from the TAPISTRY clinical trial in patients with RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer and ARROW trial in patients with RET fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). 
      • At the 2026 American Thyroid Association (ATA) Annual Meeting, HR-QOL among patients with medullary thyroid cancer and RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer from the ARROW clinical trial of pralsetinib was presented in an oral session, demonstrating that treatment with pralsetinib resulted in clinically meaningful improvements in several measures of HR-QoL for patients, including diarrhea, a common symptom of patients with medullary thyroid cancer and RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer. In addition, data from the ARROW and TAPISTRY clinical trials of pralsetinib in patients with RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer showed robust and durable clinical activity, with an overall response rate of 83.7% and a median progression-free survival of 30.3 months. The safety profile was consistent with previous experience and monitoring for infections is warranted.

      Third Quarter and Year-to-Date 2026 Financial Update

      For the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, total revenues were $80.9 million, consisting of $72.3 million in net product sales and $8.6 million in contract revenues from collaborations. Net product sales increased 13% compared to $64.1 million in the same period of 2025. TAVALISSE net product sales were $46.0 million, an increase of 3% compared to $44.7 million in the same period of 2025. REZLIDHIA net product sales were $9.9 million, an increase of 20% compared to $8.3 million in the same period of 2025. GAVRETO net product sales were $9.8 million, a decrease of 11% compared to $11.1 million in the same period of 2025. VEPPANU became commercially available from Rigel in August 2026 and generated initial net product sales of $6.6 million. Contract revenues from collaborations primarily consisted of $3.8 million from Grifols S.A. (Grifols) related to earned royalties and delivery of drug supplies, $3.2 million from Kissei Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Kissei) related to delivery of drug supplies, and $0.3 million from Medison Pharma (Medison) and a total of $1.3 million from other parties related to earned royalties and delivery of drug supplies.

      Total costs and expenses were $63.8 million, compared to $41.0 million for the same period of 2025. The increase in costs and expenses was primarily driven by higher research and development costs related to the R289 and vepdegestrant clinical programs, cost of product sales, commercial-related expenses due to the commercial launch of vepdegestrant, and personnel-related costs.

      Income before income taxes was $17.4 million, compared to $27.6 million for the same period of 2025.

      Rigel reported net income of $13.2 million, or $0.70 basic and $0.65 diluted per share, compared to $27.9 million, or $1.55 basic and $1.46 diluted per share, for the same period of 2025.

      For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total revenues were $218.4 million, consisting of $194.2 million in net product sales and $24.2 million in contract revenues from collaborations. Net product sales increased 17% compared to $166.6 million in the same period of 2025. TAVALISSE net product sales were $130.6 million, an increase of 15% compared to $113.3 million in the same period of 2025. GAVRETO net product sales were $30.1 million, a decrease of 6% compared to $31.9 million in the same period of 2025. REZLIDHIA net product sales were $26.9 million, an increase of 25% compared to $21.4 million in the same period of 2025. VEPPANU became commercially available from Rigel in August 2026, and net product sales were $6.6 million. Contract revenues from collaborations primarily consisted of $10.8 million from Kissei, including a $4.0 million regulatory milestone and delivery of drug supplies; $10.5 million from Grifols related to earned royalties and delivery of drug supplies; and $0.9 million from Medison and a total of $2.0 million from other parties related to earned royalties and delivery of drug supplies. Contract revenues from collaborations in the prior year period included $40.0 million in non-cash revenue resulting from the release of the remaining cost share liability from Rigel's collaboration agreement with Eli Lilly and Company (Lilly) and a $3.0 million regulatory milestone in connection with the approval of TAVALISSE in the Republic of Korea.

      Total costs and expenses were $165.8 million, compared to $122.2 million for the same period of 2025. The increase in costs and expenses was primarily driven by higher research and development costs related to the R289 and vepdegestrant clinical programs, cost of product sales, personnel-related costs and commercial-related expenses due to the commercial launch of vepdegestrant.

      Income before income taxes was $52.7 million, compared to $99.1 million for the same period of 2025.

      Rigel reported net income of $39.1 million, or $2.11 basic and $1.97 diluted per share, compared to $99.0 million, or $5.52 basic and $5.38 diluted per share, for the same period of 2025. As noted above, the prior year period included $40.0 million in non-cash revenue related to Rigel's collaboration agreement with Lilly.

      Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments as of September 30, 2026 was $99.3 million, compared to $155.0 million as of December 31, 2025.

      2026 Outlook

      Rigel has updated its 2026 total revenues guidance to approximately $290 to $295 million, from the previous range of approximately $285 to $295 million, which includes:

      • Net product sales of approximately $255 to $260 million, from the previous range of approximately $255 to $265 million.
      • Contract revenues of approximately $35 million, from the previous guidance of approximately $30 million.

      The above revenue guidance excludes VEPPANU. 

      The company also continues to anticipate it will report positive net income for the full year 2026, while funding existing and new clinical development programs.

      Conference Call and Webcast with Slides Today at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time
      Rigel will hold a live conference call and webcast today at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time (1:30 p.m. Pacific Time).

      Participants can access the live conference call by dialing (877) 407-3088 (domestic) or (201) 389-0927 (international). The conference call will also be webcast live and will be accessible from the Investor Relations section of the company's website at www.rigel.com. The webcast will be archived and available for replay after the call via the Rigel website.

      About ITP
      In patients with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), the immune system attacks and destroys the body's own blood platelets, which play an active role in blood clotting and healing. Common symptoms of ITP are excessive bruising and bleeding. Patients suffering with chronic ITP may live with an increased risk of severe bleeding events that can result in serious medical complications or even death. Current therapies for ITP include steroids, blood platelet production boosters (TPO-RAs), and splenectomy. However, not all patients respond to existing therapies. As a result, there remains a significant medical need for additional treatment options for patients with ITP.

      About AML

      Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a rapidly progressing cancer of the blood and bone marrow that affects myeloid cells, which normally develop into various types of mature blood cells. AML occurs primarily in adults and accounts for about 1 percent of all adult cancers. The American Cancer Society estimates that there will be about 22,720 new cases in the United States, most in adults, in 2026.2

      Relapsed AML affects about half of all patients who, following treatment and remission, experience a return of leukemia cells in the bone marrow.3,4 Refractory AML, which affects between 10 and 40 percent of newly diagnosed patients, occurs when a patient fails to achieve remission even after intensive treatment.5 Quality of life declines for patients with each successive line of treatment for AML, and well-tolerated treatments in relapsed or refractory disease remain an unmet need.

      About NSCLC

      It is estimated that over 229,000 adults in the U.S. will be diagnosed with lung cancer in 2026. Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in the U.S., with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) being the most common type accounting for 77% of all lung cancer diagnoses.6 RET fusions are implicated in approximately 1-2% of patients with NSCLC.7

      About ER+/HER2-, ESR1-mutated Metastatic Breast Cancer
      Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women in the United States, except for skin cancers.8 The estrogen receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (ER+/HER2-) patient population represents the majority (70%) of breast cancer, where treatment with endocrine therapies (aromatase inhibitors) is the standard of care. While endocrine therapy remains a cornerstone of metastatic ER+/HER2- breast cancer treatment, up to 50% of patients treated with endocrine therapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor acquire estrogen receptor 1 gene (ESR1) mutations, resulting in endocrine resistance and poor prognosis. Treatment options in second-line and later ER+/HER2-, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer setting include chemotherapy, selective estrogen receptor degraders (SERDs), and as of May 2026, vepdegestrant, the first and only FDA-approved oral PROteolysis TArgeting Chimera (PROTAC).

      About TAVALISSE®
      TAVALISSE (fostamatinib disodium hexahydrate) is indicated for the treatment of thrombocytopenia in adult patients with chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who have had an insufficient response to a previous treatment.

      Please click here for Important Safety Information and Full Prescribing Information for TAVALISSE.

      About REZLIDHIA®
      REZLIDHIA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a susceptible isocitrate dehydrogenase-1 (IDH1) mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test.

      Please click here for Important Safety Information and Full Prescribing Information, including Boxed WARNING, for REZLIDHIA.

      About GAVRETO®
      GAVRETO is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic rearranged during transfection (RET) fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) as detected by an FDA-approved test and adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with advanced or metastatic RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer who require systemic therapy and who are radioactive iodine-refractory (if radioactive iodine is appropriate).*

      *Thyroid indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s).

      Please click here for Important Safety Information and Full Prescribing Information, including Boxed WARNING, for GAVRETO.

      About VEPPANU™
      VEPPANU is indicated for the treatment of adults with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative, estrogen receptor-1 (ESR1)-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer, as detected by an FDA-authorized test, with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy.

      Please click here for Important Safety Information and Full Prescribing Information for VEPPANU.

      To report side effects of prescription drugs to the FDA, visit www.fda.gov/medwatch or call 1-800-FDA-1088 (800-332-1088).

      TAVALISSE, GAVRETO and REZLIDHIA are registered trademarks and VEPPANU is a trademark of Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

      About Rigel
      Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: RIGL) is a biotechnology company dedicated to discovering, developing and providing novel therapies that significantly improve the lives of patients with hematologic disorders and cancer. Founded in 1996, Rigel is based in South San Francisco, California. For more information on Rigel, the Company's marketed products and pipeline of potential products, visit www.rigel.com.
